items.title: Depart for Astropolis with the Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.5 Trailer
Honkai Star Rail x ROSTIC'S collaboration launched in Russia - animated trailer unveiled
items.summary: The event will be gradually rolled out in different cities.
items.content:
1 15 August 2026, 22:37 Boris Piletskiy The event will be gradually rolled out in different cities.

The creators of Honkai Star Rail announced in August the start of a collaboration with ROSTIC'S in Russia. An animated trailer was unveiled to celebrate the launch of the event. According to the plot, Castoria and Phaenon were tasked with: "pleasing players with a delicious and exclusive combo."

Initially, the collaboration was launched in Moscow and St. Petersburg ROSTIC'S – where "Express Combos" in collaboration with Honkai: Star Rail appeared.

On August 18, the launch is expected in other Russian cities, including: Yekaterinburg, Krasnodar, Irkutsk, Nizhny Novgorod, Omsk, Rostov-on-Don, Tyumen, and Volgograd.

Players will be able to get collectible items with Honkai Star Rail characters, as well as a promo code for in-game bonuses:

Main treasures: a collectible keychain with Phaenon or Castoria in blind boxes and an in-game promo code when ordering in the mobile app or at a self-service kiosk with authorization. Источник изображения: VK community ROSTIC'S Recently, Honkai: Star Rail developers held a special stream dedicated to update 4.5 and talked about future plans. For example, miHoYo (HoYoverse) confirmed the HSR collaboration with another of its games – Zenless Zone Zero.

HoYoverse had revealed Honkai: Star Rail's Version 4.5 update, " To Roll the Stars in Astropolis ," during a livestream on August 14, 2026. The patch goes live globally on August 26 for PC, PlayStation 5, iOS, and Android, picking up the story with a trip to Astropolis, two alternate character variants, a new racing event, and a dialogue speed toggle for cutscenes and quest conversations.

Following the Express Crew's victory over Lord Ravager Asat Pramad in Planarcadia, the Voracity plunges the region back into crisis. To find the strength needed to help Planarcadia survive, the Trailblazer departs for Astropolis, a key Interastral Peace Corporation stronghold in the Epsilon system that doubles as the IPC's entertainment headquarters and its executives' vacation resort of choice. The story combines political maneuvering through the IPC's upper hierarchy with a summer vacation alongside Robin and Aventurine, unfolding sometime after the events in Planarcadia conclude.

Robin Summeretto debuts as a 5-star Wind character on the Path of Remembrance. Having taken over the Oak Family since Sunday's departure from Penacony, she secretly uses her time in Astropolis to investigate Gopher Wood's legacy. In battle, she sings alongside her memosprite bird band, buffing the team while accumulating Vibes from allies' actions, building toward a Fever Pitch state that strengthens further the more often her allies act.

Aventurine Waveflair, a 5-star Quantum character on the Path of Elation, leans into a surfer and beach volleyball aesthetic while quietly working to confirm his suspicions about a traitor among the Ten Stonehearts. The first-half Event Warp pairs the limited 5-star Light Cone "Rise and Sing" and 4-star Light Cone "A Little Getaway" with a rerun banner for Hyacine. Aventurine and his signature Light Cone, "Summer Rides the Surf," follow in the second half alongside a rerun for Ashveil.

The headline event, "Overdrive: Whirlwind Grand Prix," puts the Trailblazer in charge of a racing crew as team principal. Version 4.5 also adds the "Minuscule Great Adventure" stage event, a Divergent Universe refresh, and the returning "Planar Fissure" and "Realm of the Strange" double-drop events. Players can also unlock the Trailblaze Fashion headwear "Aw, Look Up Here." HoYoverse confirmed a Honkai: Star Rail x Zenless Zone Zero crossover for later in 2026.

Honkai: Star Rail – May this journey lead us starward

items.title: "Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.5 "To Roll the Stars in Astropolis" is Coming Soon"
items.summary: 'To Roll the Stars in Astropolis' content will make sense to players who love a bit of Waveflair in the summer.
items.content:
SINGAPORE, August 14, 2026 — Global interactive entertainment brand HoYoverse announced today that the new Version 4.5 of its title Honkai: Star Rail, "To Roll the Stars in Astropolis," will officially launch on August 26, 2026. Facing a crisis triggered by the Voracity, the Trailblazer will officially depart for Astropolis, a key Interastral Peace Corporation stronghold, to seek aid for the disaster-stricken Planarcadia. In addition, the Trailblazer will have the opportunity to embark on a special summer vacation with Robin and Aventurine. Click to watch the Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.5 trailer: https://youtu.be/hTIdycp-c9Y Click here to access the media kit: https://hoyoverse.box.com/s/61n3qpa5t60i6smrkc3gxxp1xc3uka3d Following the Express Crew's victory over Lord Ravager Asat Pramad, the Voracity makes THEIR official appearance, once again plunging Planarcadia into a fatal crisis. To find the crucial strength needed to aid Planarcadia, the Trailblazer will attempt to evade the Voracity's obstruction and officially depart for Astropolis, the headquarters of the Interastral Peace Entertainment. There, the Trailblazer will navigate the complex hierarchy of the IPC's upper management to secure the key power required to help Planarcadia survive this calamity. As the crown jewel of the IPC's business empire, Astropolis not only embodies the elegant lifestyle of Interastral Peace Corporation workers and executives, but also serves as the vacation destination of choice for countless envoys, tycoons, and officials from across the Pan-Cosmic Trade System. In the story of this Trailblaze Continuance, which takes place either shortly or a long time after the journey in Planarcadia concludes, the Trailblazer will embark on an unforgettable interstellar vacation in Astropolis alongside Robin and Aventurine. In this update, the 5-star Wind character on the Path of Remembrance, Robin • Summeretto, will officially debut. Since Sunday left Penacony, Robin has taken over as the head of the Oak Family. This time, Robin isn't just here to perform, but is also on a secret mission to investigate Gopher Wood's "legacy." However, this superstar's stage isn't limited to concert venues. In combat, Robin • Summeretto will also take the stage and sing alongside her little bird band, providing buffs for the team. At the same time, her teammates' actions will accumulate Vibes for Robin • Summeretto. After she uses her Skill and her Vibes reach a certain level, her voice will bring the team to a Fever Pitch. Whenever allies attack the enemy, they will gain buffs, and the more frequently allies take action, the stronger the buffs Robin • Summeretto provides. Furthermore, when Robin • Summeretto uses her Ultimate, she can make a designated teammate immediately take action and regenerate Energy, while simultaneously increasing her own Vibes. It's also worth noting that in this story, Robin • Summeretto will debut her brand-new single, Only by Chasing the Wind, delivering a summery burst of vitality and surprises to fans in Astropolis and across the cosmos! In the second half of the version, the 5-star Quantum character on the Path of Elation, Aventurine • Waveflair, will make his debut. Despite kicking off a leisurely vacation in Astropolis, Aventurine continues to secretly leverage his connections and bargaining chips, vowing to verify his conjectures about the traitor among the Ten Stonehearts one by one. As a sports enthusiast and avid surfer, Aventurine • Waveflair attacks enemies in combat using a beach volleyball or by surfing the waves. Whenever he uses an ability or a teammate takes action, Aventurine • Waveflair can accumulate Punchline and Fervor. When Fervor reaches a certain number of points, he immediately triggers an extra Elation Skill. This not only attacks all enemies but also deals multiple instances of random single-target DMG. During the next Aha Instant, Aventurine • Waveflair's Elation Skill is further enhanced. The more actions the team takes, the higher the DMG dealt by the Elation Skill. After the version update, the drop rate for the limited 5-star character Robin • Summeretto and the limited 5-star Light Cone "Rise and Sing" will be boosted. The limited 5-star character Hyacine will concurrently receive a rerun, and the 4-star Light Cone "A Little Getaway" will also be added to the first half's Event Warps. Starting September 12, the drop rate for the limited 5-star character Aventurine • Waveflair and the limited 5-star Light Cone "Summer Rides the Surf" will be boosted, and the limited 5-star character Ashveil will also receive a rerun. In terms of version events, the racing event "Overdrive: Whirlwind Grand Prix" will officially kick off! The Trailblazer will step up as a team principal, leading their crew to become the brightest new stars on the track. Additionally, the "Minuscule Great Adventure" event will be launching simultaneously, allowing the Trailblazer to experience some fun and relaxing stage challenges. At the same time, the Divergent Universe is getting a gameplay update. The "Planar Fissure" and "Realm of the Strange" double-drop events, alongside a brand-new piece of Trailblaze Fashion, the electronic emoti standee headwear "Aw, Look Up Here," will all be going live as well. As for the story mission experience, starting from Version 4.5, story dialogue can be sped up. Players can toggle this feature on or off at any time during story dialogue. Finally, Honkai: Star Rail has officially announced its collaboration with MOONDROP. Sparxie-themed collaboration products and various online and offline events will gradually roll out across multiple regions worldwide, with more details to be revealed soon. Later this year, Honkai: Star Rail will also launch a surprise collaboration with Zenless Zone Zero. Characters from the world of Zenless Zone Zero will join the Trailblaze on a cosmic adventure, so stay tuned for more details! Honkai: Star Rail is now available on PC, iOS, Android, Epic Games Store, and PS5™, and has officially exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms. In 2023, the game won Apple's App Store iPhone Game of the Year, Google Play's Best Game, and BEST MOBILE GAME by The Game Awards. In 2024, it received the Golden Joystick Awards Still Playing Award (Mobile) and PlayStation Partner Awards 2024 PARTNER AWARD among other honors. The game has been rated Teen by the ESRB and is also classified as PEGI 12. For more details and updates, please visit https://hsr.hoyoverse.com/ or follow @HonkaiStarRail on Twitter (X), Instagram, and Facebook. About Honkai: Star Rail Honkai: Star Rail is a space fantasy RPG title with a journey through immense worlds of the unknown. The player takes on the role of "Trailblazer," a courageous individual implanted with a powerful artifact, Stellaron, and bearing the determination to unravel the mysteries surrounding the fabled "Cancer of All Worlds" and Aeons. The game features fantasy elements with myths and legends integrated into the space sci-fi story. Combined with the intuitive turn-based combat system, diverse and distinctive companions, and immersive storylines that together compose an interstellar melody filled with captivating worlds, each brimming with unique cultures, awe-inspiring landscapes, and mythical wonders to explore. About HoYoverse HoYoverse is committed to providing immersive virtual world experiences to players around the world. We have brought fans popular games including Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, Honkai Impact 3rd, Tears of Themis, and Zenless Zone Zero, as well as a wide range of entertainment content. Community is at the heart of everything we do. We are devoted to engaging fans and fostering an enthusiastic and inclusive global community that provides access and encouragement for people to share their passion for ACG (Animation, Comics, and Games) through their own creativity and skills. Pushing the boundaries of imagination, we consistently explore cutting-edge game development technologies, and have accumulated leading technical capabilities in cel shading, cloud gaming, and other fields. In the future, we will continue to expand our content production, technology research, and publishing duties through operations in offices in Singapore, Montreal, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Seoul, and other areas. UGREEN x Honkai: Star Rail Yao Guang Gift Box Impressions
items.summary: UGREEN created a collaborative effort with Honkai: Star Rail to give us a lot of new phone accessories inspired by the game.
items.content:
About a month ago, UGREEN announced a collaboration with HoYoverse on its gacha game, Honkai: Star Rail . The collaboration itself focused on Yao Guang, a character in the game. After doing the write-up and reaching out to the PR team about the products, I was fortunate enough to get a shipment of them to look at for myself. I was pleased with a lot of what I was able to try out.

I was given the full gift set alongside the power bank to look at. Honestly, the way this gift set looks is amazing. It has a peacock display of feathers when you open the box, which gives it an amazing first impression. I was incredibly surprised at how well it was put together.

The presentation of the Gift Set is good and all, but what is included? The big-ticket item, in my opinion, is the external battery charger. It has a 10,000 mAh capacity, which essentially means that, for me, it can charge my phone to full two times. As long as the battery has at least half a charge, I don’t need to charge it to keep my phone fully charged.

It is also worth noting that there is a magnetic ring so it can connect to phone cases with magnets inside. The main use case for these accessories is tailored to newer iPhones. With that in mind, I use a Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra. I was pleasantly surprised that the battery still connects magnetically to my phone. Even if you don’t have a magnetic phone case, there is a USB-C cord attached to the charger.

The next two items go together. One of the first things I noticed while opening the case was the weird circular object inside it. This is a USB-C to USB-C cord that can expand and retract. I will admit, I thought it could expand farther than it was able to, but it has the length it does because it is meant to be portable. You are meant to put it in a bag or in your pocket, and it is small enough to fit.

I would not recommend putting too much pressure on it or moving around whatever you are charging with the cord. It likes to retract if it feels like it can. It’s best to let it charge something and just leave it alone until it’s fully charged.

The part of the gift set this complements, though, is the power brick! The power brick looks beautiful, honestly. It is a nice shade of blue, and it has a picture of Yao Guang on it. It supports 65W charging, which makes for a pretty fast charging speed. Granted, the cord and the device need to be able to handle that too. Yes, the USB-C cord in the gift set supports that charging power. It actually supports up to 100W charging.

I mentioned that the gift set is tailored to iPhone products. The next part of the set shows this the most out of all these devices. It is the tracker. It essentially works like an Apple tag. You can pair it with the app, and you will be able to see where the tracker is whenever you open it.

I do not have an iPhone, but my wife does, so I had her see how easy it was to set up. Basically, you can use the Find My app and sync the tag with it in just a few seconds. It is recommended to put it on car keys or a purse, so if those get lost or stolen, you can find them pretty easily.

The smaller items in this list are more cosmetic than any of the others. The first one is a nice pin that shows off Yao Guang. I didn’t attach it to anything, but I do like how it looks. It will probably go into my other pins and stamps collection.

Then we have what I call the bookmark. It is a pretty hefty piece of hard paper. They call it a ticket on the website , meant to be reminiscent of the tickets in Honkai: Star Rail that you use to summon characters. I think a good use for it is as a bookmark, though!

Last but not least, the remaining items included in the gift set are the acrylic standee and the actual bag to hold everything in. First is the acrylic standee. It is not just Yao Guang that is included with this, as you also get a little stand behind her that adds feathers to her model.

One thing that is very much a part of her character is the peacock feathers, so the people designing that standee knew it was necessary to add them to her design, even if it meant adding an extra part to the acrylic standee. There is also a small bag included that can fit all your travel items. This way, you won’t need to fill your pockets with a lot of these little items. Plus, it means you are less likely to lose something small.

That was everything included in the Honkai: Star Rail X UGREEN Gift Set, but there is one other thing included in the actual collaboration. This is sold outside the gift set, likely because it is the thing most people will buy individually. That item is the power bank.

items.title: Giving a game another chance
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it. That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I...
items.content:
Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it.

That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I had to stop playing because of bugs. I also stopped because it was really laggy, but I realized when I started playing again this past December that I had actually originally played on the European server rather than the American one, which was why it was lagging.

Now that I’ve started playing it again for the last four months, I’m wishing I’d never quit.

The game’s story is amazing. With games like HSR where the main character is a self-insert, I tend to fully lean into that role. As such, whenever a major twist happens to a character that the main character has bonded with, I really feel it due to the immersion.

Another thing I like about the story is that HSR keeps you on your toes because it isn’t afraid to kill off playable characters.

I’d played a different game from HoYoverse before HSR, and it wouldn’t dream of killing a playable character, so I went into HSR thinking it’d be the same. That idea went out the window on my second day of playing with the first of many playable character deaths.

Because of that, you end up wanting to make sure you own your favorite characters in case you never see them in the game again. However, since HSR is a gacha game, you’re not guaranteed to get the characters you want when they’re available without spending money.

At least that’s what you’d think, but from my experience, HSR is the easiest gacha game I’ve played when it comes to getting the characters you want without spending money.

I’ve managed to get three characters I’ve wanted along with two of their exclusive items without spending money. That’s because HSR makes it really easy to get the in-game currency for pulling characters. That means if you just want to get a character for the sake of having them, you can.

In fact, I’d say HSR is probably the only gacha game where you don’t have to spend real money. I only spent money on cosmetics, but most cosmetics are free rewards from permanent events.

The only negative thing I have to say about the game is that the newer main quests are fairly long.

The latest finished questline takes 62 hours to complete, and the entire main quest line is currently over 100 hours. Because of that, if you have a busy daily schedule, it could take a while to complete. It is possible to finish in a week, but based on personal experience, I wouldn’t recommend it.

The length aside, I would highly recommend this game, especially since it’s free on PC and you don’t even need a gaming one as I play on my laptop. With the three years of content in the game so far, I can’t wait to see where it goes from here.

items.title: Hands on with the Honkai: Star Rail v4.0 experience
items.summary: This HoyoVerse train just keeps on chugging!
items.content:
The last article I wrote for Honkai: Star Rail was going over the details of the upcoming Version 4.0 release . Since then, HoYoverse generously offered up the opportunity to play Version 4.0 and experience Planarcadia early. Having spent about a dozen hours or so playing with the new characters, experiencing the story, and generally taking in the sights and sounds of Planarcadia, I’m prepared to share my thoughts on all of it.

It’s best to start off with the main attraction of Version 4.0: Planarcadia. This new planet is a fictional world come to life and boy does it leave a fantastic first impression. Full of the kind of sights and sounds you’d expect from an Asian city brimming with life. Exploration is a blast with all the alleys and little nooks to find, the platforming segments that can either help you navigate across certain parts of the city or find chests within them. There’s also a new style of puzzles that require you to rotate a 2D plane in a 3D space to “paint” certain parts of it to make them solid and let you platform with those objects. Planarcadia is so full of whimsy and still has some of the overhang of a crime family really enabling a super unique feeling planet compared to what we’ve had with previous locations such as the Xianzhou or Amphoreus.

The two new characters following the path of Elation feel great, even if the Aha Moment is a little overstimulating sometimes. Sparxie and Yao Guang fit on a team together like a glove to demolish all the bosses I’ve thrown them against. I’m eager to see where the new path goes with time, especially since we only have the two characters currently. Even as of the live public server branch, we’re unsure when Elation Trailblazer will make their debut, so keep an eye on that as versions progress beyond 4.0. You’ll need to get a hold of new Elation Light Cones as well since they obviously can’t use the other Paths’ options. Burning skill points to increase the Elation stacks until Aha decides he’s satisfied and steps in for a big attack feels really great and it has me curious what future Elation characters might do when they trigger their own Aha Moments.

Not to mention that for new players, you’ve got the opportunity to really kickstart a team of your choice with a new planet. We’re at a point in the game where there’s so many options for characters you can pick from and build around, and 4.0 introducing Elation means that as a new player, you can jump in and get a headstart on pulling for that archetype. Especially with a new Novaflare round of buffs, there’s even more options than before bringing older characters back into the limelight. The Black Swan and Sparkle buffs are so massive that people running DoT teams or any team using an action advance support such as Bronya or Sunday have another insane option. Sparkle was always good, but her Novaflare enables her to further buff your DPS units to extreme levels. Black Swan’s Novaflare was even more insane and rocketed her back up to the top for damage even as a DoT unit. Combined with the option to pick a free character including units like Sparkle, Kafka (who works great in DoT teams), and more, you really can’t go wrong in Planarcadia and the Version 4.0 patch from what I’ve gotten to experience.

Between the free characters, the great change of pace in the story from the latter half of Amphoreus (if you’ve played it, you know), the new cityscape that is quite honestly my new favorite location in the game, and all the new characters to look forward to, you really should make a return to Star Rail if you’ve been away for a minute and are curious about where we’re at. If you’re new, definitely consider giving it a shot. There’s even a bonus to let you convert trace materials for leveling character skills at a 1 to 1 ratio this time instead of a 2 for 1, so you really can kickstart your Elation team. With characters being important again like Silver Wolf, Blade, and Himeko, as well as new faces like Sparxie, Yao Guang, Ashveil, and Pearl, I think 4.0 is just the start of a real treat of a patch cycle for Honkai: Star Rail.

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail 4.0 impressions
items.content:
I'll admit, I recently burned out on Honkai: Star Rail. Upon hearing the news that 3.8 would be the lengthiest patch yet and with content more sparse than ever before, I decided to take a break for the first time since I started playing all the way back in 1.0. The entire Amphoreus saga left me feeling drained; I thoroughly enjoyed 3.0-3.4 as excellent set-up chapters, but felt lost as the plot became a labyrinth of hidden motivations, layered twists, hours of exposition, and endless proper nouns. When looking at the story as a whole, I love the characters (Aglaea and Anaxa in particular) and the rich history of the world within the Scepter, but the later patches often felt like studying for a needlessly convoluted test. I understood the gist of what was happening, but I won't lie to you and say I could describe to you in detail what Cyrene's deal is or how Evernight fits into everything.

All that's to say: I was looking forward to the Astral Express crew taking a well-earned vacation to Planarcadia, the planet of Elation. Despite two of the game's four current versions ostensibly beginning with Akivili's disciples deciding that they need a break from the backbreaking work of saving the universe, neither has resulted in our trailblazers seeing much downtime. Unlike previous excursions, it's all hands on deck: everyone gets off at this stop (save for Black Swan's incredibly hasty and unfortunate exit prior to departure). It's fun to see the entire main cast get involved, none more welcome than Himeko — up until now, the only character trait I could've told you about her was that she's terrible at making coffee. Getting some elaboration on her backstory and giving her a personality outside of "Express mom" is long overdue.

The Trailblazer and March 7th begin their Planarcadian getaway with a suitably devious greeting by none other than our old pal Sparkle. We're given a tour of the vibrant, totally-not-Japanese-inspired streets, crawling with humans living in tentative harmony with totally-not-Penaconian-memetic-entities known as imagenae. Here, we catch a glimpse of what I hope will become one of Planarcadia's core themes: gentrification and the plight of capitalism, with a side of anti-imperialism (all perpetrated by the IPC, of course). It's bold, though, and I worry that future patches will keep these criticisms in the background rather than highlight them as Planarcadia's core issues. I would love so much for little nuggets of lore to be elaborated upon, ones that suggest a more serious political history than Aha would have you believe: what did the imagenae do before the IPC forced them to integrate into society? Were they not allowed to work at all? Were they marginalized and seen as second-class citizens? Is the Department of Aberration Defense an inherently evil organization left to determine on their own which imagenae deserve their continued existence and which do not? Is Kuchiba so hot that it doesn't even matter?

This brings us to the Synwish Syndicate, a gang formerly designed to be a respite for imagenae that feel rejected elsewhere, now, due to IPC intervention, a gang that largely exists to enable monetary gain by questionable means. Here at the syndicate's headquarters, the plot quickly begins to balloon into what feels like a collection of introductions for what's to come. We have Pearl's cold and calculating grip on the planet, Himeko and her confounding family history, the potential return of the Herald of Death, the Stellaron Hunters' unknown involvement in the Phantasmoon Games, Sunday's inadvertent entry into the Games, Evanescia's whole...thing, and Yao Guang's bottomless supply of divinations. What's most shocking is that the patch still manages to pull off a fun (if bloated) self-contained story, adding layers to one of HSR's most inscrutable characters and ending things with one of the game's best low-stakes twists.

I'm no Xianzhou Arbiter-General, but I can pretty easily peer into the future and divine a prophecy for Honkai: Star Rail: each new patch will introduce and/or discuss at length a new prophecy that cryptically divulges the fate of a character and/or planet and/or simulation masquerading as a planet. It's hard to pinpoint the moment a theme becomes a crutch, but I think HSR passed that moment long ago. In this patch, we have not one, not two, but three central characters that are defined by their relationship with prophecy and prediction — Yao Guang, Pearl, and the perennial mystery that is Elio and his script. So many in-game conversations devolve into the interpretation of prophecy, and frankly, it's becoming exhausting. We went through an entire version in which each Chrysos Heir had a poetically vague predetermined fate, and before that (and in 3.8's ret-con-y confusion) we had Sparkle's ambiguous "three deaths" for Firefly.

If this were a wholesale replacement for well-executed foreshadowing, we would have a far bigger issue. It's obvious, though, that the writing team knows how to tell a story sans-prophecy, evident in Sparkle's character-driven narrative in this very patch. Sparxie being the "true" Sparkle (as much as old Sparkle is also the "true" Sparkle) is teased so perfectly; the reveal is obvious in retrospect while being difficult to predict with the given information. It's consistently groan-inducing to see this writing cheat code being used ad nauseam within a story that could function better without it. I hope I'll be proven wrong and the game will subvert the words of its murky prophets, leaving me with egg on my face come the conclusion of this leg of the Express' journey.

4.0 is a promising new beginning, and has at the very least brought me back in terms of its story. Though there is an abundance of new proper nouns to memorize and a bevy of new and returning cast members to keep track of, the patch still takes on a welcome return to simplicity and levity (save for the shocking tonal shift right at the end, RIP the Synwish Syndicate Feb. 2026 - Feb. 2026). As long as things don't get too bogged down in extensive metaphors and tiresome exposition, I'm hopeful that Planarcadia can become the most focused version of HSR we've seen so far.
